item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00419","decision":"none","candidate_ranking":["C21","C16","C20"],"selected_candidate_label":null,"confidence":0.9,"relationship_type":"none","rationale":"The three strongest candidates concern civil defense, but none plausibly supplied a concrete and material drafting template for the later memorandum. C21 is closest because it directs every Federal department and agency to prepare civil-defense and continuity plans, yet its planning machinery, consultations, approvals, and coordination provisions are materially different from the child's short directive requiring Washington-area agencies to participate in a particular exercise. C16 discusses the importance of civil-defense planning and coordination with local governments, but it is addressed to one board and assigns broad planning leadership rather than ordering agency participation in an exercise. C20 establishes and empowers the Federal Civil Defense Administration; its general cooperation clause is routine and not reproduced in the child. The shared subject and generic government-wide directive language are insufficient.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"each Department and Agency of the Executive Branch of the Federal Government in the Metropolitan Area of Washington participate in the Civil Defense Exercise","parent_excerpt":"each Federal department and agency shall, in consultation with the Federal Civil Defense Administration, prepare plans","explanation":"C21 shares the civil-defense setting and an agency-wide command, but changes from preparing emergency plans under a detailed statutory framework to participating in one dated exercise; there is no distinctive shared wording or parallel operative sequence."},{"child_excerpt":"The need for effective civil defense planning is still vital to our national welfare. But national plans and preparations are of little value without active participation at local community levels.","parent_excerpt":"a definite necessity to continue planning for civil defense... call upon the other agencies of the Government and to consult with representatives of the States and local governments","explanation":"C16 contains the nearest conceptual combination of civil-defense planning, other federal agencies, and local participation, but its language and administrative action are too different to establish reuse as a drafting template."},{"child_excerpt":"I continue to urge all Departments and Agencies to prepare for these exercises to the fullest extent possible.","parent_excerpt":"All departments and agencies of the Federal Government are authorized and directed to cooperate with the Administrator","explanation":"C20 also calls for government-wide cooperation in civil defense, but this is a routine cooperation clause within an order establishing an administration, not material language or machinery carried into the exercise memorandum."}]}
